checks.detail: Both source modules were read in full, including active-Finset wrappers and all exact line-parameter/inner-product wrappers.
The cone carrier is the actual finite nonnegative sum, with proved zero/generator membership and addition/scaling closure.
Each nonnegative coefficient is bounded by Cauchy--Schwarz divided by the genuinely positive strict-polar gap; no coefficient bound is a supplier.
Finite coefficient boxes are compact; a convergent physical-sum sequence has a convergent coefficient subsequence and its limit represents the same physical limit. Closedness is proved, not assumed.
Closedness only uses finitely many coefficients in a compact finite product; it does not silently require ambient finite dimension or linear independence.
The complete-space bipolar theorem is instantiated with proved cone nonemptiness and proved closedness.

The finite strict-polar Farkas statement uses actual nonpositive tangent inequalities and follows from genuine separating hyperplanes. Negation and real inner-product symmetry give the required outward orientation.
Active-Finset wrappers are exact subtype/sum translations with no cardinality-three or simplicity hypothesis.
Vacuous finite families and zero coefficients are handled by actual finite sums; positivity assumptions requiring an active slope correctly preclude an empty clipping index.
A finite nonempty negative-slope set supplies the minimum of actual a_i/(-b_i) ratios. The selected intercept is strictly positive because old-zero slopes vanish.
Positive-slope/nonnegative-slope and negative-slope cases retain every original finite inequality; no inactive tuple or constraint is dropped.
The negative clipping endpoint is obtained by reflecting all slopes, with the correct positive new slope and negative time.
alpha=tplus/(tplus-tminus) and beta=-tminus/(tplus-tminus) are positive, sum to one and cancel the line displacement.
Every point between the actual endpoints is feasible by checking the correct endpoint for each slope sign.
Old zeros remain zeros and each endpoint has an active constraint with genuinely nonzero slope, which is sufficient for the later two-level polar argument.
The original physical vector is exactly the positive weighted sum of the two endpoint vectors, by module algebra.
A nonzero direction orthogonal to the sum of spanning generators has a nonzero slope somewhere, hence both strict slope signs because their sum is zero.
The final split is the same scalar construction evaluated at actual inner products, including every feasibility, old-zero and vector-decomposition conclusion.
